column1: # clues.tsv for ft_strcapitalize — hints only, never answers.

A "word" begins right after any non-alphanumeric character (or at the very start of the string). The first letter of a word becomes uppercase; every other letter becomes lowercase. How can you tell you are at a word boundary by looking at the PREVIOUS character?
Digits are alphanumeric too. So in "42abc", does the digit count as part of the word -- is 'a' a word start or not? And what about a digit sitting in the middle of a word?
